note: Olli asked for a different card content style rather than further positional tightening: centre-aligned in-card content, with a bigger centred Wings mark and the public name / extended name stacked beneath it. He explicitly authorised partial occlusion on the cards tucked behind their neighbours in exchange for a better-looking mark on the whole -- a deliberate relaxation of the full-legibility requirement that bounded Rounds 08 and 10.

sections.title: Hero
sections.feedback: Centre-aligned versions of the in-card content. Make the Wings bigger and have them centred, then have the titles under that. I don't mind if a bit of it gets cut off on the others -- it's more about making it look better.

constraintSupersession.priorConstraint: Rounds 08 and 10 treated 'every card's public name must remain fully legible under hit-testing' as a hard requirement that bounded how tight the fan could compact.
constraintSupersession.supersededBy: Olli's explicit statement that partial occlusion (cutoff) on the tucked-under cards is acceptable, in service of a cleaner and bigger centred mark on the whole family.
constraintSupersession.scope: This authorisation applies to occlusion caused by the fan's own overlapping cards, not to accessibility, contrast or rendering failures -- those remain governed by the existing static-twin, reduced-motion and WebGL-failure fallbacks.
constraintSupersession.implementation: The hero identity mark moved from bottom-left anchored to fully centred (horizontally and vertically) within each card, with a larger Wings icon and larger title type. Ecosystem-shelf and final-route cards, which use the same shared component, are unchanged. The overlapping fan geometry itself (per-card step and horizontal overlap) is unchanged from Round 10.
